A1-A2.headline: Exploring the Vast Lands and History of Canada

pages.text:
Canada fills the top half of North America. It is the second-largest country on Earth, reaching from the Atlantic to the Pacific and Arctic.

Most people live in southern cities. The cold north stays quiet and wide open.
pages.caption: Historical poster representing Canadian identity and service.

imageProvenance.credit: Unknown lithographer. Adapted from photo by Brown Bros.
imageProvenance.imageAttribution: Unknown lithographer. Adapted from photo by Brown Bros. (Public domain)

evidence.articleCaption: English: They serve France. How can I serve Canada? Buy Victory Bonds.

pages.text:
Native peoples have lived on this land for thousands of years. First Nations, Inuit, and Métis groups built strong towns and wide trade roads.

The country's name comes from an old word, kanata, which means village. In 1535, local people shared that word with French traveler Jacques Cartier.

In the 1500s, French and British groups reached and settled the east coast. After long wars, France gave up most of its North American lands by 1763.

A big change came in 1867. Three British lands joined together as one union. That step built modern Canada from four early parts.

Canada is a free country led by an elected prime minister. A royal figure serves as head of state through a local official.

Ottawa is the capital. Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver lead business and culture.
pages.caption: Aerial view of the Canadian Parliament Buildings in Ottawa.

evidence.fileTitle: File:Parliament Hill from a Hot Air Balloon, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada, Y2K (7173715788).jpg
evidence.articleCaption: Aerial view of Canadian Parliament Buildings and their surroundings

pages.text:
In recent years, Canada has grown very diverse. Its population passed forty million people, helped by open entry plans for newcomers.

Shared respect and human rights stand at the heart of modern Canadian life.

B1-B2.headline: Understanding the Geography, History, and Governance of Canada

pages.text:
Stretching across northern North America, Canada is Earth's second-largest country. It spans the Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic with the longest coastline.

Most citizens live in cities, leaving the cold north sparse.

pages.text:
Indigenous peoples have lived across Canada for thousands of years, building settled towns and wide trade routes. These groups include First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities.

Canada's name stems from the St. Lawrence Iroquoian word kanata, meaning village. Local people shared it with French explorer Jacques Cartier in 1535.

From the 16th century onward, French and British groups settled the Atlantic coast. After long wars, France gave up most of its North American colonies by 1763.

A turning point came in 1867. Three British colonies joined through Confederation, forming Canada as a federal union of four provinces.

Canada runs as a parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy. The prime minister leads with support from the elected House of Commons.

Ottawa is the capital, while Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver lead trade.

C1-C2.headline: Geographical Scale and Constitutional Evolution of the Canadian State

pages.text:
Spanning northern North America from the Atlantic to the Pacific and Arctic, Canada constitutes Earth's second-largest territory and longest coastline.

Sharing the longest land border with the United States, its population clusters southward.
pages.caption: Archival wartime poster promoting national bonds.

imageProvenance.credit: Unknown lithographer. Adapted from photo by Brown Bros.
imageProvenance.imageAttribution: Unknown lithographer. Adapted from photo by Brown Bros. (Public domain)

evidence.articleCaption: English: They serve France. How can I serve Canada? Buy Victory Bonds.

pages.text:
Indigenous civilizations—encompassing First Nations, Inuit, and Métis peoples—inhabited contemporary Canada continuously for millennia, sustaining complex societies and extensive commercial networks.

The nation's etymology derives from the St. Lawrence Iroquoian term kanata, signifying village, which inhabitants relayed to French navigator Jacques Cartier in 1535.

Commencing in the sixteenth century, rival French and British expeditions colonized the Atlantic seaboard. Following protracted imperial conflicts, France ceded most North American territories by 1763.

A foundational milestone arrived in 1867 when three British colonies unified through Confederation, inaugurating a four-province federal dominion poised for continental autonomy.

Rooted in the Westminster tradition, Canada combines parliamentary democracy with constitutional monarchy under a prime minister and governor general.

Ottawa governs politically while Toronto, Montreal, and Vancouver drive commerce.
pages.caption: Aerial view of Ottawa's parliamentary precinct.

evidence.articleCaption: Aerial view of Canadian Parliament Buildings and their surroundings

pages.text:
Demographic shifts have established Canada among Earth's most pluralistic nations, surpassing forty million residents via immigration and refugee resettlement.

Multiculturalism and human rights underpin its mixed-market economy.
